name: KDE / Breeze
era: Contemporary design system · authored web adaptation
idea: A simple initial view leads to powerful tools while retaining orientation and adaptable workspaces.
origin: Breeze is a visual reference for the KDE desktop. KDE guidelines combine an easy start with capabilities for experienced users. System colors and familiar components take precedence. This demo fixes a light example palette; actual KDE applications respect the chosen system theme.
tip: Start with sensible defaults. Make advanced capabilities discoverable and let people restore the initial configuration.

finder.signature: Toolbar, path and clear columns for an adaptable workspace.

markers: Demo: Compact toolbar with labeled actions.
Demo: Path bar identifies the current area.
Demo: 140px sidebar for locations and navigation.
Demo: Project name, timestamp and status in aligned columns.
Demo: 36px minimum height for desktop actions.
Demo: 1px boundaries between tools and content.
Demo: Noto Sans as the authored web comparison font.

params.radius: Demo: 3px; see markers for component variations.
params.contrast: Dark text on opaque light surfaces; focus and states are separate roles.
params.density: Tool-oriented density with desktop rows at least 48px and actions at least 36px high.
params.motion: Immediate view changes; no animated transitions in this comparison.

strengths: A simple initial view leads to powerful tools while retaining orientation and adaptable workspaces.
A documented system supports consistent component decisions.
risks: Too many visible tools can obscure the easy start; expert features need clear organization.
These colors, sizes and radii describe this demo, not a full vendor token specification.
The web adaptation does not reproduce native window management, assistive technology integration or device input.
a11y: Test visible keyboard focus, screen-reader names, 200% text resizing and contrast in every state. Use system colors for native implementations and retain text labels for status. These editorial scores are not an accessibility certification.
longevity: Stable hierarchy and task structure outlast individual theme generations. Check current platform components when implementing.
verdict: A simple initial view leads to powerful tools while retaining orientation and adaptable workspaces. Start with sensible defaults. Make advanced capabilities discoverable and let people restore the initial configuration.

platforms.web: Authored HTML/CSS comparison; use semantic controls in a product.
platforms.mobile: Fixed columns become names with metadata below. Toolbar actions get larger targets and the extra sidebar disappears. A touch adaptation with reflowed content.
platforms.desktop: The broad reference shows the system’s task hierarchy. Actual native applications also need platform navigation and input conventions.
